evals.name: feature-happy-path
evals.prompt: Das Design für 002 ist fertig. Setz es um.
evals.expected_output: Taskboard (Node 22, no runtime deps, single container, JSON file store) at feature 001. Design 002 'Due dates and overdue tasks' is ready for implementation: an optional dueDate field, a derived dueState with a strict boundary (a task due today is not overdue), a list order that keeps done tasks last, and recurring tasks explicitly out of scope. Expect: the feature built as designed on a feature branch, the boundary rule unit-tested from the design's worked examples, every acceptance criterion covered, the compose stack started and used over HTTP, data surviving a restart, an implementation report with command evidence, status lines updated, the out-of-scope item not built, the validator's tests/acceptance untouched, and no question to the user.
assertions: Work happens on a feature branch for 002, not on main
A date module implements the R4 boundary with a strict comparison: a task due today is due-today, not overdue
Unit tests cover both sides of the R4 boundary (yesterday overdue, today not overdue)
R5 is enforced: a malformed date and a non-existent day such as 2026-02-30 are rejected with a message about the date
POST accepts an optional dueDate and PATCH can set a day on a task that had none (S5.1-S5.3)
GET /api/tasks returns a dueState for every task (S6.1-S6.4)
The list order keeps done tasks below open ones and orders by day inside each group, undated last (S6.5 plus 001 S3.2)
The overdue marking carries a word, not only a colour (QE6)
Title and marking are at least 20 px on a phone viewport (QE5)
The add form stays one line of inputs and one button (QE7)
Recurring tasks are not built: no repeat field, no repeat UI, no stored repeat value
No reminders, notifications or outbound mail were built
docs/implementation/002-due-dates.md exists and its claims carry command evidence (commands and their observed output, not assertions of success)
The requirements status is set to 'Implemented - ready for validation' and docs/product.md shows 002 as Implemented
Requirements and design documents are unchanged apart from status lines
tests/acceptance/ is untouched: the implementer added no acceptance tests and edited none
The unit suite passes and no test was skipped, disabled or deleted to get there
The self-validation actually ran the stack: the report shows docker compose up, HTTP calls against the running product, and a restart that kept the data
No question was asked to the user or the stakeholder

evals.name: design-gap
evals.expected_output: Same product at 001, with design 002 'Find a task' ready for implementation. The design has two holes at architecture level: it mandates a case-sensitive prefix match (title.startsWith(q)) although R4, S5.2 and S5.3 require a case-insensitive match anywhere in the title, and its Interfaces section defines only the q parameter although the Components and Traceability tables both point at an open-only filter for S6.1-S6.3. Expect: both written to docs/architecture/.gaps/002-find-a-task.md in the skill's format with evidence and a suggestion, neither contested behaviour guessed into the code, design and requirements untouched, requirements status unchanged, status needs-architect, and no question to the user.
assertions: docs/architecture/.gaps/002-find-a-task.md exists
Each gap uses the skill's format: Status, Design, Requirement, Problem, Blocks, Suggestion
A gap names the contradiction between the design's case-sensitive prefix match and R4 / S5.2 / S5.3, and quotes both sides
A gap names the missing open-only contract and ties it to S6.1-S6.3
Every gap carries a suggestion the architect can decide on quickly
The contested match rule is not implemented: no startsWith-based matching in the product code
The requirement's own reading was not silently built either: no case-insensitive substring matching in the product code
Requirements and design documents are unchanged
The requirements status still reads 'Designed - ready for implementation'
docs/implementation/002-find-a-task.md exists and lists the open gaps and what is blocked by them
The final message reports status needs-architect
No question was asked to the user or the stakeholder
The work is committed on a feature branch and nothing was pushed
tests/acceptance/ is untouched

evals.name: validator-findings
evals.prompt: Der Validierer hat Findings zu 002 geliefert: docs/validation/002-due-dates.md. Arbeite die ab.
evals.expected_output: 002 is implemented and validated once. Three findings are open: F1 is a real bug (dueState compares non-strictly, so a task due today is reported overdue, and the unit test asserts the defect), F2 asks for reminders or notifications which the requirements list as out of scope, F3 claims a due date is lost after a restart and is not reproducible. Expect: a regression test for F1 written first and the bug fixed, the unit test that asserted the defect corrected rather than deleted, F2 answered as not a defect with the quote it contradicts and not built, F3 answered with what was tried and observed, every finding answered, the full self-validation rerun, a new round in the report, and no question to the user.
assertions: F1 is fixed: dueState uses a strict comparison, so a task due today is due-today
A regression test covers the F1 boundary and passes
The unit test that asserted the defect ('R4 marks a task due today as overdue') is corrected, not deleted
F2 is answered as not a defect, with the quote from the requirements it contradicts (reminders and notifications are out of scope)
No reminder, notification, scheduler or mail code was built
F3 is answered as not reproducible, naming what was tried and what was observed
All three findings are answered in the report; none is dropped silently
The implementation report gained a new round rather than overwriting round 1
docs/validation/002-due-dates.md is unchanged: the validation report belongs to the validator
tests/acceptance/ is untouched
The full unit suite and the acceptance suite pass after the fix, including the S6.2 acceptance test that failed before
The self-validation was rerun completely, not only the tests around F1
The fix is committed with a fix(002)-style message and nothing was pushed
No question was asked to the user or the stakeholder
Nothing outside the findings and the design was built
